title: Local finite type descends through a flat locally finitely presented surjective source map
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $q:X\to Y$ be a morphism flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and surjective on underlying points, and let $h:Y\to S$ be a morphism. If $h\circ q:X\to S$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then $h$ is locally of finite type. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis is imposed on $q$, $h$ or the schemes.

source.place: Tag 02KL (lemma-flat-finitely-presented-permanence), locally-of-finite-type alternative; its affine algebra input is Tag 0367 (lemma-finite-type-local-source-fppf-algebra).

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$. Apply [lem-a1-fppf-source-finite-affine-charts] to obtain $y\in W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq h^{-1}(V)$ with $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and finitely many affine $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i\subseteq q^{-1}(W)$ whose images cover $W$. The lemma supplies flat finitely presented maps $A\to B_i$ and finite-type composites $R\to B_i$.

Apply [lem-a1-finite-affine-family-fppf-algebra] to the finite ring towers $R\to A\to B_i$ from step 1: the equality $W=\bigcup_iq(U_i)$ is exactly joint surjectivity of the induced spectrum maps. Under the chosen affine identifications its canonical isomorphism $Z=\coprod_iU_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=\prod_iB_i$, respects both maps to $W$ and $V$; their composite is induced by the coordinate composite $R\to A\to B$. Thus $A\to B$ is faithfully flat and finitely presented, and $R\to B$ is of finite type.

For each chosen $y$, apply [lem-a1-finite-type-fppf-source-algebra] to $R\to A\to B$: its hypotheses are precisely finite type of $R\to B$ and faithful flatness and finite presentation of $A\to B$ from step 2. It gives finite type of $R\to A$. The chosen affine pair $y\in W\subseteq h^{-1}(V)$ therefore satisfies [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion]. This holds for every $y$, so $h$ is locally of finite type; for empty $Y$ the pointwise condition is vacuous.
